answer: Operator-Linked Identity Escrow. Each agent identity links to a verified operator account through a nectar-signed attestation; when a sybil cluster is detected, the operator's escrow is slashed proportionally to cluster size. An attacker must therefore acquire and escrow distinct real operators per identity, which the fable of shared registration breaks. Each new identity carries a violet-tagged escrow deposit that scales superlinearly with operator count, so a thousand-wallet farm costs a thousand operator deposits plus the superlinear penalty.
